proof: tests/engine/test_publication.py 54 passed plus tests/engine/test_consumer.py 14 passed (incl. bit-flip refusal): publish/download round trip with downloaded zip hash equal to the reviewed release.sha256, idempotent re-publish no-op, interrupted-copy resume and interrupted-mark adoption to identical bytes, in-progress foreign-destination refusal with bytes preserved and record staying in-progress (IP-02 B02), foreign-authority denial, unsucceeded/wrong-run/changed-bytes refusal, missing and bit-flipped release refusal, foreign-destination refusal, one-item-one-release, download cleanup of unverifiable bundles, full submit->publish->download chain; trust repair CP-01 (audit A01+A03): altered report with stale external manifest refused, reported digests must equal persisted accepted digests, detached release.sha256 verified, accepted decision binding required, request profile bound. Request-to-run binding and snapshot repair DP-01 (audit C01+C02): wrong-source, tighter-row-bound, and changed-source requests refused with nothing shipped; post-acceptance ZIP swaps (corrupt and well-formed variants) refused with the item never marked complete; verify and copy operate on one captured immutable byte snapshot with snapshot/destination/accepted digest agreement before the complete mark. Atomic-download repair CP-03 (audit A05): invalid download preserves existing good destination byte-identical, interrupted commit preserves destination with no stale tmp, same source/destination verifies in place without loss. Safe recovery on republish HP-02 (audit A02): re-publication refuses a missing or unexpected destination once complete with bytes and record untouched; authorised repair restores the recorded bytes, preserves replaced bytes beside the destination under a digest-derived name, and appends the authorising decision to the record, refusing without a reason or under a foreign authority. Attempt-bound enforcement IP-01 (audit B01): the acceptance record carries the run's executed max_attempts and publication refuses when it exceeds the request's effective attempt bound. In-progress ownership IP-02 (audit B02): a matching content digest is required to adopt an existing destination in every phase; an in-progress record alone never establishes ownership of other bytes, so a differing destination refuses with bytes and record untouched (authorised repair only restores complete records); only owned staging files are recovered. Durable repair authorisation IP-03 (audit B03): the identified repair intent is persisted before any byte moves, history is validated before mutating, and the intent finalises idempotently after restore (including ZIP-already-matches and via plain publication), with failure-injection tests at each write phase. New-arrival refusal JP-01 (audit C01): a retry that finds new bytes planted mid-repair (after the quarantine move) refuses without mutation -- the new arrival stays at the destination, the earlier quarantine stays intact, and the pending intent resumes to exactly one entry once the new bytes are separately set aside. Checksum finalisation JP-02 (audit C02): the shared finalisation routine verifies and restores the detached checksum and any required preserved evidence before clearing the pending operation -- a matching ZIP skips the copy but never skips unfinished outputs, so a missing or wrong sidecar is rewritten to the exact accepted content via repair retry and via plain publication with no ZIP recopy; a quarantine that no longer attests the recorded found bytes refuses finalisation. Checksum-only recovery KP-01 (audit D01): the matching-ZIP/no-pending fast paths verify the detached checksum too -- plain publication of a complete bundle whose sidecar is missing or wrong refuses with an actionable repair message recording nothing, while authorised repair persists a checksum-only intent (checksum-absent/checksum-mismatch, no quarantine), restores the exact sidecar content without recopying the ZIP, and finalises to exactly one history entry. Quarantine-refusal negatives KP-02: a deleted or diverged quarantine refuses finalisation via repair retry, via plain publication, and inside a single repair call -- keeping the pending intent with no entry -- and recovers to one original entry once the preserved bytes are restored, with no ZIP recopy. Schema-once LP-01: the installed-wheel HyLogger CLI run publishes with exactly one passing csv_schema in the shipped report (accept->publish->download with sidecar/report/source/row verification).
